channel.name: Beyond Orbit
channel.niche: Faceless space & universe documentaries — black holes, exoplanets, cosmic scale, unexplained signals — narrated over real NASA/ESA public-domain imagery
channel.audience: USA viewers who binge space documentaries and 'what if' cosmic scenarios
channel.cta: Subscribe — a new deep-space story every week.
channel.comment: LONG-FORM space documentary channel (16:9). This is the watch-hours engine: Shorts feed watch time does NOT count toward the 4,000-hour YPP threshold, but long-form watch time DOES. Each long-form video also spawns one vertical Short (see 'shorts' below) for discovery/subs. To re-brand, change name/handle/tagline/cta here AND the channel name on YouTube.

topics.comment: Topics come from topics/space_bank.json (50 hand-written viral angles, each with a hook, script beats, chapters and suggested NASA visuals). If GEMINI_API_KEY is set and use_gemini=true, the script is expanded/fresh-written per run using the bank entry as the brief (falls back to the built-in beat templates on any error). order='sequence' walks the bank 1,2,3...; 'random' picks no-repeat random.

script.comment: 7-LAYER HOOK SYSTEM. The cold open must shock — NO logo, NO 'hey guys', NO intro. The promise states what the viewer gets by the end. open_loop_every_seconds plants an unresolved question every ~55s so leaving feels like missing something. words_per_minute=150 is the natural edge-tts documentary pace, used to estimate runtime from word count. HOW LENGTH IS ACHIEVED: the topic bank stores a BRIEF (a hook plus research beats), not a finished script, so a writer model is required. The prompt asks for a per-SECTION word budget rather than only a total, because models anchor on that far better — asking for '1500 words' produced 758. If a draft still comes back short, expand_short_scripts=true gives it one expansion pass that asks for more depth (mechanism, numbers, what is measured vs inferred, the competing explanation) and is only accepted if the result is genuinely longer. min_publishable_minutes=5 is the floor: below it generate.py SKIPS the topic WITHOUT burning it from the rotation. The floor exists to block the offline template mode, which only reaches 2-3 minutes because padding terse beats out locally would be pure filler — and filler destroys retention and is exactly what the inauthentic-content policy penalises. A 5-minute model-written script is real prose and does count toward the 4,000 watch hours, so it is worth publishing; a 2-minute stub is not. Set allow_short_publish=true only if you deliberately want short videos out.

tts.comment: edge-tts = free Microsoft neural voices, NO API key. For documentaries keep rotate_voices=FALSE — one consistent narrator voice builds channel identity (the opposite of Shorts, where rotation avoids 'templated content' flags). rate='+4%' is a calm documentary pace (Shorts use +14%). pitch='-2Hz' adds a little authority. Andrew/Brian are the most documentary-sounding US male voices.

video.comment: 1440p (2560x1440) is the DEFAULT and recommended — YouTube encodes 1440p and above with the better VP9 codec, so even a viewer watching at 1080p sees a sharper picture than a 1080p upload. resolution='4k' works but free runners have NO GPU: 4K at preset='fast' takes ~45-90 min and at preset='medium' can exceed the 6-hour job limit. shot_seconds_min/max = PATTERN INTERRUPT: the visual changes every 4-8s so attention never settles. ken_burns adds slow zoom/pan to stills so NASA photographs never look like a slideshow. GROWTH SETTINGS: best_shot_first opens on the highest-resolution asset, because the first frame decides whether anyone watches at all. end_card_seconds=12 overlays a subscribe card over the final ~12s of REAL footage (not a static frame, which is where viewers leave) — YouTube end screens can only be placed in the last 5-20 seconds, so outro_seconds was raised from 6 to 14 to make that window exist. Without this the video simply stopped with no ask, which is the single biggest lever on subscriber conversion left unused.

captions.comment: For LONG-FORM, burn_in defaults to FALSE — burned-in captions look amateurish on a 12-minute documentary and cover the visuals. Instead a real .srt track is uploaded to YouTube: better for accessibility, and YouTube indexes the text for search. Set burn_in=true only if you specifically want them baked in. The colours here are shared with the Short's burned-in karaoke captions; size and position for those live under shorts.captions_* because a vertical frame needs completely different values. enabled=false disables the .srt track entirely.

chapters.comment: YouTube requires the FIRST chapter timestamp to be 00:00, at least 3 chapters, and each one 10 seconds or longer — if any of those is violated it silently ignores the whole list. Those three rules are enforced in modules/script_writer.chapter_timings and are not configurable, because they are YouTube's, not ours. Chapters raise watch time (viewers jump back to sections) and add keyword surface to the description.

thumbnail.comment: 1280x720 is the YouTube standard. max_words=5 — on a phone a thumbnail is about 120px wide, so more than 5 words is unreadable, and unreadable means unclicked. Space thumbnails win on SCALE CONTRAST (tiny Earth beside a huge object) since there is no face to use. frame_samples=9: rather than grabbing frames at fixed timestamps (which regularly landed on a dark or empty shot and cost click-through directly), nine candidates are sampled across the film and SCORED on luminance spread, colour saturation, edge energy and mid-brightness, then the best 'variants' are used. Variant 1 is uploaded automatically; the others are saved beside it so you can swap one in from Studio if the first underperforms.

shorts.comment: Shorts are the DISCOVERY engine (subscribers); long-form is the WATCH-HOURS engine, because Shorts feed watch time does NOT count toward the 4,000-hour YPP threshold. IMPORTANT — 'count' vs 'daily_count'. count=0 means the documentary no longer has Shorts cut out of it; Shorts now come from their own daily run (generate_shorts.py + .github/workflows/shorts.yml), which builds daily_count=3 standalone Shorts from the topic bank's beats. THIS SPLIT IS A QUOTA DECISION, not a stylistic one. The YouTube daily quota is 10,000 units: videos.insert costs 1,600, captions.insert 400, thumbnails.set 50. So a documentary is 2,050 units and each Short is 1,600. Cutting Shorts from the documentary forced them all onto the documentary's own day, capping the channel at 4 Shorts that day (2,050 + 6,400 = 8,450; a 5th would hit 10,050 and FAIL) which is only about 1.7 Shorts/day. Giving Shorts their own day gives: documentary day = 2,050 + 3x1,600 = 6,850, Shorts-only day = 4,800 — both well under 10,000, and a real 3 Shorts/day. Content needs no new authoring: each of the 50 topics has 4-7 beats and one beat is ~40s of narration, so the bank already yields ~250 Shorts and grows with every topic added. publish_hours_et [12, 16, 19] = noon, 4 PM and 7 PM Eastern, spreading the three daily Shorts across the US afternoon and evening peaks.

nasa.comment: NASA content generally is NOT subject to copyright in the US — that is this channel's unfair advantage: real space imagery with effectively zero Content ID risk. SOURCE: 'images_api' (images-api.nasa.gov) only. It needs no key and is a documented stable endpoint. You may add 'svs', but nasa_fetch.py deliberately does not download from it: its JSON endpoint is not a versioned public API and a silent shape change would break every render. FOUR FILTERS are enforced: (1) block_keywords rejects the NASA logo/insignia/meatball/worm, which may NOT be used because it implies NASA endorses this channel — word-boundary matched so 'wormhole' and 'sealed' are not false positives; (2) any asset naming a third-party rights holder is skipped, since some NASA pages embed licensed music or contractor footage; (3) filter_relevance rejects institutional photos — NASA's library is an ARCHIVE, so searching 'black hole' also returns press conferences, award ceremonies, buildings, cleanrooms and mission patches, which make a documentary look like a corporate slideshow; it also requires a positive space-imagery signal; (4) min_image_width keeps low-resolution thumbnails out. IF A NICHE QUERY RETURNS TOO LITTLE, fallback_queries are tried next — these reliably return spectacular real imagery, and a genuine Hubble nebula in a black-hole Short is still real space. allow_pexels_filler is FALSE on purpose: Pexels has no real astronomy imagery, so 'black hole' there returns sci-fi renders and neon abstracts, which is exactly what made early Shorts look fake. ESA/Hubble and ESO material is CC BY 4.0, so attribution is auto-added by modules/metadata.py.

youtube.playlist_description: Deep-space documentaries built from real NASA and ESA mission imagery. A new one every week.
youtube.comment: category_id 28 = Science & Technology. TIMING: publish at 2:00 PM ET on Thu/Fri/Sat — that single slot catches the US after-school/after-work window, the 7-11 PM ET evening peak, AND the next morning. CRITICAL: upload_lead_hours=5 means the file is uploaded 5 hours BEFORE publish time as PRIVATE with status.publishAt set. Without this a 1440p/4K video goes live while YouTube is still processing, so the first hour — the single most important hour for the algorithm — is served at 360p. title_hashtags: only the FIRST 3 hashtags render above the title, so we pick deliberately.
